summary: NASA has awarded Blue Origin a $700 million contract to build a new Mars orbiter designed to establish a dedicated communications network at the Red Planet. In military developments, Gen. Schiess was sworn in as the U.S. Space Force’s highest-ranking uniformed leader as Chief of Space Operations, while the U.S. Army awarded a $192 million contract to Palantir and Anduril for the TITAN ground station program. Commercial space activity saw China complete the successful debut launch of its private, reusable Pallas-1 rocket, India send an Earth-imaging satellite toward geosynchronous orbit, and York Space Systems unveil a new satellite platform for very low Earth orbit operations. Internationally, Europe and Japan’s joint BepiColombo mission is preparing to begin its arrival sequence at Mercury after an eight-year interplanetary voyage, though the first planned private mission to Venus faces delays while awaiting launch vehicle readiness. On the debris mitigation front, Astroscale selected Isar Aerospace to launch a future orbital cleanup mission. In space science, NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope has identified a novel 10-sided decagon cloud structure encircling Saturn’s south pole, and researchers reported preliminary findings that may offer the first direct evidence of dark matter. Looking ahead, observers should watch for NASA's scheduled coverage of the upcoming launch and docking of the Russian Progress 96 resupply spacecraft.
